newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - Oct 3.

text.p: NEW YORK - The Dow industrials and other stock indices pushed to session highs in active mid-afternoon trading as money continued to rush into the market.
The Dow eased back in late trade to be 21.99 up at 5926.89 after hitting record ground at 5937.
The Nasdaq Composite erased losses from the past two sessions and climbed 13 to 1234, ever closer to June 5's record closing high of 1249.15.
Winners beat losers 15-7 on NYSE volume of 321 million shares.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 sailed through the 4,000 mark with ease on Wednesday to close at a new record peak for the second day running as a strong international bond market and Wall Street strength pushed blue chip prices higher. The FTSE 100 ended at 4,015.1, up 22.9 points.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade sharply higher after DAX index hit a new record high at 2,680.10 points, buoyed by overnight Wall Street gains and higher dollar, profit-taking failed to appear during bourse ahead of Germany's holiday on Thursday but chance for slippage in IBIS dealings. The 30-share DAX index ended up 20.77 points to 2,676.50. In post-bourse
trade the DAX index stood at 2,685.29 up 30.95.

PARIS - French shares closed higher on Wednesday in robust volume, bolstered by firm bonds, strength on Wall Street and buying by U.S. investors, traders reported. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 18.63 points at 2,141.84.

ZURICH - Swiss shares lost steam towards the end of the session as profit taking set in after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) failed to overcome a resistance level around 3,765/70 points. The Broad SPI ended up 0.52 percent, or 12.38 points, at 2,407.14.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended marginally firmer after wandering narrowly in both positive and negative territory for most of the day, most investors were on the sidelines due to a lack of incentives to buy, despite the Dow's overnight rise to a record high. The 225-issue Nikkei average closed 35.63 points or 0.17 percent higher at 21,498.60.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks snared another 1996 closing high, despite some profit-taking after recent gains, as investors remained bullish on the outlook of the market. The Hang Seng index closed 30.66 points higher at 11,951.88, the highest close since February 4, 1994.

SYDNEY - Australian shares stormed home to their highest close in five months as a flood of afternoon buying interest, inspired by surging share price index futures, pushed turnover above the A$1 billion mark. By the close the All Ordinaries index jumped 29.1 points to 2,314.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares jumped on Wednesday boosted by powerful bull markets all around the globe and a stronger rand. Dealers said strong gains on Wall Street and Britain's FTSE-100 index had provided the impetus behind the rise. A stronger rand and a recovering bullion price had been the icing on the cake to a good day's business, they added. The

overall share index ended at 6,997.1, up 100.9 points in strong volumes, while industrials jumped to 8,204.2, up 70.1 points. A bullion price struggling bravely to breach the $380 an ounce barrier also boosted golds and meant that the gold index posted the biggest gain of the day, up 3.26 percent or 54.6 points to 1,731.8.
